savings.reason: Read the complete original EO:13028, both held actor contexts, and the full EO:13345 sections 1-7. Section 6 unconditionally revokes the parent EO:12757 and EO:13028; no savings, accrued-rights preservation or exception continues this order's operative force. Successor foreign-affairs delegations and Board rules in EO:13345 sections 1-5 rest on that new order and do not save the former order. The judicial-review limitation concerns rights under this order and does not independently continue the revoked delegations or amendment commands. The bounded OFR later-instrument and eCFR searches are adequate for this no-order claim; no affirmative revival or residual lead is present.

research_rationale: Read the complete official original EO:13028 and full EO:13131 and EO:13345 actor texts. The corrected inventory retains each operative section 1 amendment (two preamble changes, three section 1 changes, redesignation, and the new prospective section-571 reference rule) and the independent section 2 judicial-review limitation, without duplicating introductory scaffolding or including page furniture. EO:13131 is a genuine later partial amendment. In particular, its section 1(c)(4) adds FAA sections 808(a)(1)(B), 808(a)(1)(C) and 808(a)(4) to the second functions-vested sentence created by EO:13028 section 1(b)(3); it does not remove that sentence's 571(a)(2), (c) and (d) delegation or Council/State requirements. Its sections 1(c)(1)-(2) expand the first delegation sentence while retaining the section-571(a)(1) insertion, and section 1(b)(2) adds a preamble law reference at the same anchor while retaining the earlier section-571/Public Law 104-107 reference. These nonterminating partial amendments are expressly recorded in the affected clauses' later_events using the full exact dossier actor-context evidence, because the short machine actor provision captures only the title/preamble lead and omits section 1(c)(4). EO:13131's present amendment language and full July 22, 1999 dating, with no postponement, establish that effective date; later filing and publication do not. Other EO:13131 changes affect different parent provisions and do not extinguish these retained rules. The missing-list entries are assessed individually: EO:12823 predates EO:13028 and is acknowledged as the parent's existing amendment history, so it cannot be a later end of EO:13028's independent commands; the supposed missing EO:13131 provision is substantively supplied by the complete held actor context. No own-term sunset or report deadline is present. The inserted section 6 condition on later matching statutes changes reference scope rather than ending the order. EO:13345 section 6(c), in the full actor dated July 8, 2004, says hereby revoked with no postponed date. This unconditional internal-government revocation ends all retained EO:13028 rules on July 8, rather than July 12 filing or July 13 publication. No savings continue this order; new EO:13345 assignments rest on that new authority. The OFR catalog/held-order search, supplemented by the cutoff eCFR search, supplies adequate bounded later coverage; the U.S. Code release through October 9 is not asserted as a current predicate. No conflicts or affirmative revival leads remain.
